title: Patching Debian and Ubuntu Servers
intro: Unpatched servers are how most breaches start. Patching is simple in principle, but running services keep old library versions in memory, some upgrades need reboots, and automatic updates need guard rails. Here's the full Debian/Ubuntu cycle.

steps.prompt: Refresh the package lists and list what can be upgraded.
steps.fake_output:
Hit:1 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu jammy InRelease
Get:2 http://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu jammy-security InRelease [129 kB]
libssl3/jammy-security 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.18 amd64 [upgradable from: 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.15]
openssh-server/jammy-security 1:8.9p1-3ubuntu0.10 amd64 [upgradable from: 1:8.9p1-3ubuntu0.6]
linux-image-generic/jammy-security 5.15.0.122.122 amd64 [upgradable from: 5.15.0.119.119]
steps.explanation: Security updates for OpenSSL, OpenSSH, and the kernel.
steps.why: Packages from the '-security' pocket are the ones that can't wait. The kernel upgrade will need a reboot; the others need service restarts.

steps.prompt: Check what unattended-upgrades would install tonight, without installing anything.
steps.fake_output:
Allowed origins are: o=Ubuntu,a=jammy-security, o=UbuntuESMApps,a=jammy-apps-security
Packages that will be upgraded: libssl3 openssh-server linux-image-generic
Option --dry-run given, *not* performing real actions
steps.explanation: Only security-origin packages are allowed automatically.
steps.why: unattended-upgrades is on by default on Ubuntu, for security updates only. Know what it's set to do, in particular its Automatic-Reboot settings, because an unplanned fleet-wide reboot is servers-incident-002.

steps.prompt: Hold back the postgresql-14 package so no upgrade touches the database until the planned maintenance window.
steps.explanation: Neither apt upgrade nor unattended-upgrades will change postgresql-14.
steps.why: Holds protect components where an unplanned restart or version change is costly, like databases. Track holds and review them: a hold 'for this week' that's forgotten becomes an unpatched database two years later. 'apt-mark showhold' lists them.

steps.fake_output:
The following packages have been kept back:
  postgresql-14
The following packages will be upgraded:
  libssl3 linux-image-generic openssh-server
3 upgraded, 0 newly installed, 0 to remove and 1 not upgraded.
steps.why: 'kept back' is expected for the held package. It also appears when an upgrade needs new dependencies, where 'apt full-upgrade' (or dist-upgrade) is needed; review what it adds or removes first.

steps.prompt: The new OpenSSL is installed, but running services still use the old copy in memory. List which services need a restart, in list mode.
steps.fake_output:
Pending kernel upgrade!
Running kernel version: 5.15.0-119-generic
Expected kernel version: 5.15.0-122-generic
Services to be restarted:
 systemctl restart nginx.service
 systemctl restart ssh.service
 systemctl restart app.service
steps.explanation: Three services still use the old OpenSSL, and the kernel needs a reboot.
steps.why: A library patch doesn't protect anything until the processes using it restart. That's the patching step most often skipped, which leaves the 'patched' server still vulnerable. /var/run/reboot-required existing means a reboot is pending.
